notes.title: The debugging phase begins, version 1.3 is on the way!
notes.content:
So most parts of the upcoming version 1.3.0 have been implemented. We are looking forward to a lot of debugging in the next weeks.
[h1][b]Editor[/b][/h1]
Ok, I should explain why we decided to add an ingame editor. As you probably know we added a new animation system. And this has a lot of settings. These can of course be controlled via C++ code. But this would take a lot of time, as we would need to recompile the code everytime we change something. And this takes a lot of time.

The editor will allow us to change the code while the game is running

To achieve this we implemented several sub goals:

[b]Entity creation via XML and visual programming[/b]

Normally the entities in our game are create by C++ code. This can not be changed while the game is running. So we added a system which allows the creation of entities via XML. And the XML file is generated via visual programming. So for simple entities we will no longer need to write code.

Every entity consists of modules which communicate via events. State machines are also supported.

The necessary information is collected via reflection from the C++ code. Reflection in this case means that our program can analyse it's own structure. In Java and C# this is supported by the language itself. In C++ this isn't the case (I do not understand why, it would have saved us a lot of work). We had to augmented our code with additional informations.

[b]Improved GUI[/b]

To be abled to display all the necessary information we needed additional GUI elements. So we implemented a tree view and a scroll box. We also corrected and updated the menu system.

[b]Game control[/b]

The game can be pause, started in slow motion or single steps can be triggered via the editor. Cheats are also accessible.

[b]Project viewer[/b]

We added a project viewer which displays all files which are accessible by the game.

[b]Asset viewer[/b]

And we of course have an asset viewer. Currently it displays images and entities.

But we also did other stuff:

[b]Sounds[/b]

I tried to record better environment sounds for the game. But in my home town I did not find a place where there is now noise (cars, people …). It it is really annoying if you think that we are constantly living with such a noise level.

[b]Multiplayer[/b]

I also continued with multiplayer but this is clear as the network system will also use some kind of reflection system which is similar to the one use to create the entities.

[b]Animations done[/b]

We added animations for the bear and the red deer. This are for the start basic ones.

[b]What will come...[/b]

I hope that we soon can create our own entities in the game. I am very exited.

notes.title: Milestone 1 / 4 in the creation of the new version 1.3 is achieved.
notes.content:
To make the waiting for the version 1.3 easier I thought it would be a good idea to present you our milesstones:

1. Basic Client / Server Animation System (finished)
2. Advanced parts of the Animation System (Retargeting, Inverse Kinematik, Rag Doll Animation)
3. Updating the enemy AI
4. Debugging
 
Despite this we follow a lot of minor projects which also make good progress. These are of course the creation of good animation for our enemies. And we want to introduce fluent water and a system which will help you to find the resources in the next release. 

[b]Basic Client / Server Animation System[/b]

As mentioned above the basic animation system has been implemented. On the server side we use a state machine to control the client side animations. In the last announcement we talked about problems regarding our motion blending system. We added now several methods to blend our animations:

- kth best animations
- all animations which influence the behavior above a certain threshold
- delaunay triangulation (which is very cool because it gives the best performance)

Imagine for example the running animation has a speed of 6 m/s and the walk animation has a speed of 3 m/s. If the player is then moving forward with a speed of 4 m/s then motion blending is used by taking the best fitting animations into account. 

[b]Models[/b]

And we also made progress regarding our models. To our main character we added a lot of motion capture data: different kinds of walk, jump and turn animations. She can now even make a workout in a gym (but we do not know if we really need this, but it looks so cool).

Then we optimised our meshes by removing invisible polygons and by creating low poly version of them. We also created a male model which we call guard. The only problem with this is that we planned to recycle all the animations from our main character Lisa for the guard. But as Lisa is female and the guard is male he has a different kind of skelet. This means that we cannot simply copy our animation. They have to be retarged. This can be done in Blender but it would be nice if our engine could do this because it would save memory if we would only have one set of animation loaded at runtime.

[b]Water[/b]

We finished our special water update algorithm. With this I do not mean the algorithm which calculates the water movement. I mean the algorithm which updates the actual water mesh which is send to the GPU. In our first experiments we used for this the standard world updating algorithm. But this approach was to slow. 

[b]Editor[/b]

And we started with the development of an ingame editor. This editor is first meant only to be used intern but later we plan to release it to the public so that everyone can use it to create mods for the game.

We first experimented with Qt but we did not liked the result. And it did looked a lot like the unity game editor. As this wasn't our goal we did abandoned this project.

[b]Reflection[/b]

Ok this is perhaps interesting for all of you who can program in C++. We want to be abled to analyse the structure of the classes at runtime. This is especially important for the new editor. This is called reflection. In Java and in C# it is directly supported by the language. In C++ this isn't the case. So we started with the developmemt of our own reflection api. 

[b]Delaunay Triangulation[/b]

As mentioned above we used this kind of data structure in our animation system. This was really hard to implement but it will allow us to smoothly blend between different kind of animation states.

[b]Bear[/b]
And finally the bear has a walk, run and attack animation!

notes.title: Animation System
notes.content:
Hello we just wanted to give you feedback on what we are doing. This time we do not have any screenshots because we are changing big parts of the engine. This will be also the case in the following weeks.

[b]Animation System[/b]

Except for one little problem we nearly finished the new client side animation system. For this we changed the way how we store our rotations from euler to quaternion. This will also simplify the import of models.

The new animation system will support blending and composing of an unlimited amount of animations. That means that all animations will be totally smooth. And also that the monster will be better moving on the ground. 

We also thought about adding advanced stuff like retargeting and compression of motion capture data. 

And to the little problem. In AAA games it is common to have something which is called blend space or a blend tree. This allows the easy composition of all types of animations. An example here would be walking and running. This algorithm can then calculate the animation for half walking and half running. We will also use something similar to this but we still need to decide how to calculate the amount of impact each single animation has to the final animation. For the 1D case this is trivial. For the 2D not. But of course we will find a solution.

But the cool thing is that we now need much less animations because a lot of them can be generated on the fly.

[b]Models[/b]

We recreated nearly all of the first person animations for our new character model Lisa. That means that in the next big release the black hand will disappear. The cool thing is that these animations are compatible with the third person mode. So they can be used there too. -> less work

And we collected a lot of motion capture data which we will use to create realistic motions for all our game characters. I am also thinking here about NPCs!

[b]Water flow[/b]

All physic objects are now affected by the flow of the water. We also created a special water update mode which improves the update speed.

[b]Hierarchical entities[/b]

The system now supports hierarchical enitites. That allows use to create complexe game items.

[b]Secret stuff[/b]

And I am experimenting with something really cool which will improve the gameplay (hopefully :-) ). But I will take about it later.

notes.title: Dev Blog #19 - Bug fixes, new entities and new release!
notes.content:
A new release has been uploaded to the unstable release. Here are the changes:

[b]HDR improved[/b]

The problem with the black shadows is resolved. But I am still not satisfied with the colors. I miss a little bit the summer feeling. We will improve this in further version.

[b]Wooden framework and stairs added[/b]

We added a new wooden framework set. So you can create wooden towers, stairs or even wooden platforms. Here is an example of a perch:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/screenshot90.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/screenshot89.jpg[/img]

[b]New placement indicator[/b]

As we tested the wooden framework we had problems when placing the objects on top of each other. The problem was that when the object is not placeable the engine will display nothing which makes it difficult to current the placement position. This has now been resolved. When it is not possible to place an object the game will nevertheless disable a box:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/screenshot121.jpg[/img]

Ok it's barely visible but this is intention. There should be a clear difference to the case when you can place the object:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/screenshot122.jpg[/img]

[b]Glass renderer[/b]

The last bug in the transparence renderer has been found:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/screenshot123.jpg[/img]

In this screenshot you can see 3 transparent layers: The glass in the foreground, the torch and the glass in the background!

[b]Music added[/b]

A youtuber had the idea that it would improve the atmosphere of the game when we add music. This has been done now. We are using free music from cdk downloaded from ccmixer.

The music can of course be disabled in the configuration menu.

[b]Feature overview[/b]

As youtubers often say that there isn't much to do in this game we added a feature overview when you start the game. The feature list is not complete yet. Here is a screenshot:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/screen2.jpg[/img]

[b]Bug fixes[/b]

We did a lot of bug fixing. The most annoying bug was in the shadow map generation system. When the player moved it could be that the shadow map was generated with the wrong sun position. This produced flickering. Then we removed the rest of the old game engine. As you may have noticed that it says copyright 1996- . This means that there was also an old quake style engine in this game. We removed parts of this old engine.

[b]Added entities on game start[/b]

One youtuber complained that he found it boring when it is dark at night. Ok, since the first commercial release of our game we have the „Bed“ in which you can sleep. To make it easier for newbies we added several entities when the game starts. Amoung these are a bed, torches and a chest.

[b]Compressed Data Structures[/b]

For the new world matrix we created compressed data structures. But it is still a long way!

[b]Loading of meshes optimized[/b]

And as we want to bring the bear in the game we again worked on the model importer. We imported a sheep, the fish and a dangerous insect!

[b]Helpers[/b]

I know that we had a lot of helpers amoung the players and the youtubers. Without these tipps the game would not be game as it is today. If you helped us and want to be named in the credits of the game just send me a mail: info@staudsoft.com

So that's it for today. I hope you enjoy the new version!

notes.title: Dev Blog #18 - HDR released
notes.content:
Hello guys! Welcome back!bI know it took a little more time with this post, but this is simply because we have worked so hard. We have practically rewritten every shader. I did not thought that it would be so hard to create a HDR pipeline. As a small consolation I already uploaded the new version!

And I also changed the development policy. Where we used to have multiple projects running simultaneously we will focus now on a specific goal. And that is currently HDR. The next will be the gameplay!

[b]HDR[/b]

The first pictures of the HDR pipeline just looked terrible. The colors did not match. Everything was too dark, etc. We debugged a lot but now I think it looks good. We currently only have a problem with the colors, they are very highly compressed which makes the shadows and shades look very hard. And thus has changed the tone of the game a little bit. But I still think that it's cool to finally support HDR!

Here is a picture of a sunrise: 

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen3.jpg[/img]

The night rendering is also working again. The first attempts looked terrible because the star had the same strength as the sun:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen5.jpg[/img]

[b]Glare[/b]

Glare is a phenomenon that occurs in normal life when strong light strikes the retina. This also activates light receptors which are not directly affected by the light. Here's a screenshot:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen8.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen6.jpg[/img]

And the glare of the moon is not a sprite anymore

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen4.jpg[/img]

[b]Blur[/b]

The underwater view is now blurred:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen7.jpg[/img]

We also considered whether we should use this effect when the player is poisoned.

[b]Depth of Field[/b]

For cameras or the eye not everything is always in focus. The rest is out of focus. This is also implemented now:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen9blur.jpg[/img]

The focusing has made us initial problems because we did the distance determination via raytracing. When that did not work, we have now realized the function with the graphics card.

[b]Motion blur[/b]

I have always found it so great in other games when the screen slightly blurred if you changed the viewing direction. As we were already working on the shader we implemented this too:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen2.jpg[/img]

[b]Blur at top speeds[/b]

And then we inserted an effect which makes the screen borders appear blurred at high speeds:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen10.jpg[/img]

This occurs currently only when the player falls. In later versions, when the player is able to move more quickly, we will also use this effect.

[b]New settings HDR[/b]

We added a new settings page so that you can tune the HDR effect:

HDR - On / Off
HDR adaptation speed - how fast the virtual eye adapts to the brightness.
Luminance HDR - How bright is the scene?
HDR Blur - Blur underwater
HDR motion blur - Motion blur when the player moves.
HDR Depth of Field - Depth of field
HDR Focus adaptation Speed ​​- How fast the focus of the virtual camera reacts
HDR Aperture - How big is the iris / aperture of the virtual camera
HDR Glare - How strong is the glare effect
HDR Star Effect - The effect is similar to the glare effect.
HDR FrontMotion - distorts the screen when the player is moving very quickly.

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen1.jpg[/img]

So I hope you like the improvements

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen3.jpg[/img]

The night rendering is also working again. The first attempts looked terrible because the star had the same strength as the sun:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen5.jpg[/img]

[b]Glare[/b]

Glare is a phenomenon that occurs in normal life when strong light strikes the retina. This also activates light receptors which are not directly affected by the light. Here's a screenshot:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen8.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen6.jpg[/img]

And the glare of the moon is not a sprite anymore

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen4.jpg[/img]

[b]Blur[/b]

The underwater view is now blurred:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen7.jpg[/img]

We also considered whether we should use this effect when the player is poisoned.

[b]Depth of Field[/b]

For cameras or the eye not everything is always in focus. The rest is out of focus. This is also implemented now:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen9blur.jpg[/img]

The focusing has made us initial problems because we did the distance determination via raytracing. When that did not work, we have now realized the function with the graphics card.

[b]Motion blur[/b]

I have always found it so great in other games when the screen slightly blurred if you changed the viewing direction. As we were already working on the shader we implemented this too:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen2.jpg[/img]

[b]Blur at top speeds[/b]

And then we inserted an effect which makes the screen borders appear blurred at high speeds:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen10.jpg[/img]

This occurs currently only when the player falls. In later versions, when the player is able to move more quickly, we will also use this effect.

[b]New settings HDR[/b]

We added a new settings page so that you can tune the HDR effect:

HDR - On / Off
HDR adaptation speed - how fast the virtual eye adapts to the brightness.
Luminance HDR - How bright is the scene?
HDR Blur - Blur underwater
HDR motion blur - Motion blur when the player moves.
HDR Depth of Field - Depth of field
HDR Focus adaptation Speed ​​- How fast the focus of the virtual camera reacts
HDR Aperture - How big is the iris / aperture of the virtual camera
HDR Glare - How strong is the glare effect
HDR Star Effect - The effect is similar to the glare effect.
HDR FrontMotion - distorts the screen when the player is moving very quickly.

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screen1.jpg[/img]

So I hope you like the improvements

notes.title: Development Blog #17 - Unstable Release, Plant Shader, Bear, Lisa, HDR
notes.content:
[b]Unstable Release[/b]

We found several errors in the current unstable release. So we uploaded a new version to Steam. Changelog:
[list]
	[*]Updated the light rendering system[/*]
	[*]Added a new light rendering setting[/*]
	[*]Increased the carrying limit[/*]
	[*]Fixed bug where the [u]Voxel_Lamp[/u] did not emit light without a current[/*]
	[*]The bounding box around the [u]Voxel_Barrel[/u] was corrected[/*]
	[*]Fixed crash when using the wrong game settings[/*]
[/list]
If this version works well we will upload it to the default branch.

[b]New Plant Shader[/b]

Our modeler who also studied biology had the idea to improve plant rendering. The problem with the leafs is that in the real world the light passes through them. In the old version this was not the case. This has now been changed. We wrote a special plant shader which simulates this behavior. Here are some screenshots:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screenshot81.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screenshot82.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screenshot84.jpg[/img]

[b]Updated Bear[/b]

Our modeler also optimized the bear. Ok personally I must admit that I always had the impression that this wasn't a bear. It looked like a pig for me. And the reason for this was that the neck was to long. This has been corrected. And we also added collar bones to the bear and optimized the skeleton. I personally find it crazy that such small details can hugely affect the appearance of a model. Here are some screenshots:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/bearv2.png[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/bearv2b.png[/img]

The skeleton for the bear is now finished. The armature was rigged yesterday. And today the bone weights where updated. Hmm, without good bone weights the movements of the bear look really …. unhealthy :-)

[b]Lisa[/b]

Last time one player asked if we will update the arm in the first person view soon. We want to do even more. We decided to create a complete character for our game and add third person support. For this we used MakeHuman to create Lisa.

I thought that it would be easier to create a good looking character. The first experiments looked like a bad plastic surgery. After this problem was solved we checked out several armatures which are available for MakeHuman characters. At first we used Rigify. But with this system we could not control the mouth or the eyes. So we now sticked to the basic MakeHuman armature. Here is a screenshot:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/lisa9.jpg[/img]

The clothes are basical from MakeHuman. We had to change the T-shirt and the hairs as they produced depth buffer artifacts.

We have to admit that we do not know much about her. We can only conclude some things which we see in the game. She seems to have the ability to resurrect herself when she dies. That of course also means that she is perhaps ageless. And she is then not a normal human being. Perhaps she uses nanotechnology to achieve this but this has yet to be revealed. And we do know nothing about her motives. In the current version of the game she is wearing black gloves.

[b]Mocap[/b]

We also checked out the possibility to use motion capture for the animation. A jump animation was successful applied to Lisa.

We downloaded several gigabytes of Mocap data.

[b]Additional Assets[/b]

And we also searched the internet for additional assets to improve our wild life. We found a good deer and some other animals. But if we can we will create our assets by ourselfs.

[b]HDR[/b]

The HDR rendering also makes progress. The basic pipeline is implemented. We are currently working on the basic+glare pipeline. But we did not do any bug fixing. Yeah, GPU debugger. This is not so much fun. There is also a bug in the shadow rendering algorithm which we also should find. So much work ...

[b]World Matrix[/b]

We nearly finished the final design. I do hesitate a little bit to start with the implementation because when the design is not correct the code can be trashed. So I borrowed some books about design patterns from the library. I think we will use a similar design as the I/O system in todays OS kernels. The reason for this is that we want to allow multiple threads to access the world matrix. So we can use the full power of todays multi-core CPUs.

[b]Multiplayer[/b]

Yes we also continued with this. The network description for the entity class is finished. Now the player and the world class will follow. That is part 1 of 5 of the multiplayer implementation.

[b]Test Map[/b]

As we mentioned in the previous posts we are creating a test map. This time we improved the castle. Check out the screenshots:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screenshot8.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screenshot10.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/screenshot11.jpg[/img]

[b]New Wooden Scaffolding Set[/b]

We created new entities which can be used in the creation of scaffolding:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/newelements.png[/img]

[b]Linux Pipeline[/b]

We also created a new linux pipeline in a virtual machine with Ubuntu 12.04 LTS. This is the same version which Steam uses. This will also ensure better portability with other Linux distribution. We also created special versions of the shared libraries. They will now be shipped with the game. This means it won't be necessary to install additional libraries if you want to use this game.

That was really a big post!

notes.title: Development Blog #16b - Version 1054 for Windows, Linux and Mac
notes.content:
Hey guys I just uploaded the new version to the unstable branch (with the cool graphics updates!). It comes with a Linux and Mac version.

If you want to test the Linux or Mac version you will need to change to the unstable branch. The default branch will install nothing!

Mac:

- You will need iOS 10.9. It should run out of the box. If not let me know.

Have fun!

notes.title: Development Blog #16 - Bobbing movement, better bump maps and castle
notes.content:
Hello and welcome back!

In the last we week we mostly worked on the HDR system:

[b]HDR[/b]

We created the basic architecture of the HDR system. We will implement several different types of pipelines:
[list]
	[*]Basic HDR, no glare[/*]
	[*]HDR, with simple glare[/*]
	[*]HDR, with glare, star effect[/*]
	[*]HDR, with glare, star effect and depth of field[/*]
[/list]
Of course every pipeline can be adjusted to the performance of your indiviual computer.

The engine is now abled to use a floating point buffer and supports HDR lights. In fact the only thing what is still missing is the tone mapping algorithm. This will reduce an HDR image to a low dynamic range so that it can be displayed on the screen. This algorithm will also simulate the light adaption of the human eye. But of course at a much faster rate. It would not be practial to wait 20 minutes for the virtual eye to adapt to the light strengths in caves!

[b]Bear[/b]

When the HDR system is finish we plan to update the whole enemy system. This was also the reason why we updated the model imported. And we created a bear:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/bear4.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/bear3.jpg[/img]

[b]Bobbing settings[/b]

A player had the idea that we should implement a bobbing movement when the player moves. This has been done. Check out the video:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bjTfrP8xOKc

And you can also see that we made a castle for testing purposes:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot6.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot2.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot4.jpg[/img]

We will add more stuff to the interior.

[b]Glass[/b]

As mention the next unstable release will feature glass. Here are some screenshot of the glass in action:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot76.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot741.jpg[/img]

 

[b]Improved bump maps[/b]

Along with the parallax occlusion mapping algorithm we also updated the bump mapping algorithm.

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot0.jpg[/img]

 

This nearly looks as parallax occlusion mapping was used but it isn't. This means the game will look better even if you only own an old computer.

 

[b]iOS & Linux pipeline[/b]

Both pipelines are completed now. We created release versions for both platforms. We also configured Steam for the deployment. We are currently doing a lot of testing. Especially the settings dialog makes still problems.

notes.title: Development Blog #15 - Toolchains
notes.content:
[b]iOS toolchain created[/b]

We created a toolchain which creates with one command a Mac release of our game. It was quite interesting as the search path in the dynamic libraries are statical encoded when you compile your application on a mac. They have to be changed afterwards. We hope that everything is working now and that the game will run on other Macs. Feedback is always welcome!

You should have at least iOS 10.9. It could work on older version but we are not sure as we did not tested it.

The next step is to set up Steamworks so that the game can be uploaded to Steam.

[b]Linux toolchain[/b]

We also started with the creation of a Linux tool chain. We plan to support Ubuntu 14.04 LTS.

[b]Model toolchain[/b]

Yes this is the toolchain posting :-). We also nearly finished a model toolchain which will automatically integrate our models from Blender in our game!

[b]Shader Generator[/b]

As we want to implement HDR in our game we thought that it would be the best if we create a shader generator. This little piece of software will allow us to embed the GPU code better and faster in our game. As a test we are currently implementing the Gauss filter which is used to generate the glare. With this filter other effects like depth of field would also be possible.

The generator will allow us to program the GPU in a similar way as we do it with the CPU. Perhaps this does not sound very cool if you are not a programmer but it is in fact very cool!

[b]HDR Pipeline[/b]

We created the concept for our HDR pipeline. It will support glare, depth of field, a simple form of motion blur when you move fast, light adaption, blur and night tonemapping.

[b]Colored Glass[/b]

In the next unstable release we will enable the ability to create glass. The renderer is working now with the exception that it is not compatible with the particle effects. This means you will not see a burning fire if you look through glass. But if you don't everything will be ok.

And we thought it would be fun to add colored glass, so we did it. Here is a screenshot of the germany flag made out of glass:

 

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot84.jpg[/img]

[b]Engine Reset[/b]

As mentioned last time we want the user to be able to change the screen resolution in-game. This works now as the engine is able to reset itself without a restart. And when you change the screen resolution a nice window will appear which will allow you to reset the resolution if you do not like it or if it isn't supported. We had to disable fullscreen support for the Linux and Mac version as we had problems with SDL. Under Linux the mouse does not work and under iOS the screen changed to black. And then we had to reset our Mac. These are not bugs in our game these are bugs in SDL.

[b]New World Matrix[/b]

And we started with a long term project. We want to create a new data structure which stores the voxels of our game. Our goal is to add support for multiplayer, dynamic water and a much faster world loading system. But this will take 6 – 12 months.

[b]Bad freelancer[/b]

And we tried to hire a freelancer to create some models. Unfortunately he did not told us the price and he started to model before we ordered models. And now he thinks that we will pay him money.

notes.title: Development Blog #13 - Parallax Occlusion Mapping, Shadow Mapping and Configuration Dialog
notes.content:
In the last days we did a lot. Let's start with the configuration dialog:

[b]Configuration Dialog[/b]

As mentioned last time we want to add an in-game configuration dialog. With the exception of the screen resolution every settings appears now in our new dialog. Check out the screenshots:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/space-2015-04-07-21-06-30-542.jpg[/img]

This dialog was created from annotated source code. So it should not happen again that some of these settings are not accessable. We also updated the icon for the check box and added new settings. If you want to see the dialog in "live" check out the video below.

The old configuration dialog which appears when you start the game has been deleted!

[b]Shadow rendering[/b]

As we now have moving plants we thought that it would be nice if the shadow map is also animated. In the past it was so that the shadow map was only updated every 25 frame or when necessary. So it couldn't follow the movement of the plants. So we added now a setting which allows you to enable this feature if you have a good computer. You can see it in action in the video!

And the grass does not cast a shadow any more. This only produced unrealistic artifacts.

[b]Parallax Occlusion Mapping[/b]

Ok implementing this was really crazy. I also thought about naming this post "What the heck is going on? In which coordinate system am I?". The general parallax mapping (not parallax occlusion mapping) algorithm is relative easy but you have to check in which coordinate system you are and in which coordinate system you interpolate your values. For example the view direction is essential for this method. I originally interpolated the normalized view direction which produced strange results. Then I realised that I had to interpolate the view position, then in the pixel shader create the view direction and then normalize this vector. Everything else produces strange results. But I still feel a little uncomfortable about this algorithm. There is a minus sign where it shouldn't be, but it doesn't work without it. Hmm, I feel like a guy who builds something and then realises that some screws are remaining.

Then I had the parallax mapping algorithm implemented. But it was not really noticeable and when I increased the effect it distorted the texture. The main problem was that the height map contained small details and this did not work very well. So I implemented a gaussian blur algorithm to smooth the height map which is used for parallax occlusion. It looked better but I still wasn't satisfied. So I decided let's do it all and implemented Steep Parallax Mapping, Parallax Occlusion Mapping and Relief Parallax Mapping. These algorithms perform a raycast in the tangent space of the texture. This creates the illusion that the texture has depth. Just look at the screenshots:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot721.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot73.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot71.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot671.jpg[/img]


This will be enabled for the blocky voxels. I also tested in on the trees but it didn't look good. The next thing what we have to do is to adapt the height maps so that we even get better rendering result. Check out the video:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=beXNdvrP1eQ&feature=youtu.be

notes.title: Development Blog #12 - Plants, Configuration Dialog and Rendering Engine
notes.content:
Hello and welcome back! In the last 2 days we did a lot!

[b]Parallax Mapping[/b]

As we want to add parallax mapping we started to code to bring support in our engine for this. What is parallax mapping? Normal Bump Mapping changes only the color of the surface so that it looks like it is bumpy. Parallax Mapping does also change the surface itself by change the texture coordinates depending on the view position of the player. This gives than the illusion that the texture has "depth". We implemented now the basic algorithm but we still need to do bug fixing. So no screenshots yet!

[b]Configuration Dialog[/b]

We want to add an in-game configuration dialog. This is because we want to create a MacOS version and as the combination of SDL and wxWidget which is used in the Windows version does not work well on MacOS we started to code a configuration dialog. Or more precisely we started to code a generator which will generate the configuration dialog for us! This is standard in most AAA games. So no big deal. Here is a screenshot of the dialog:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/settings.jpg[/img]

We are currently testing the different types of widgets. New is here the Hot Key Widget which will allow you to configure the keyboard settings.

This dialog was created by seven lines of code! We course have to add a lot of more. The system needs to know what to do when the settings are changed. Do we only need to set some basic variables or do we have to reset the engine or do we even have to restart the game!

[b]Normal map for the plants[/b]

I didn't liked the look of the plants. So I started to think. I wanted to give the player the impression that the plants are round and not flat. The trick with blurring the mask and then using this as the input of the normal map generator didn't looked very well. I decide to create an algorithm which generates a realistical height map out of the plant texture. To achieve this I first defined a function which calculates the distance to the nearest transparent point for every pixel. The result for a tree texture is then the following:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/distancemap.jpg[/img]

This height map can then be used to simulate tree branches. What do we need for every pixel? We need the radius of the branch and the current height of the branch. The first can be extracted by raycasting in the height map to the nearest transparent point and then taking the maximum of all encountered pixels. Of course we have to go in both direction: In the direction to the nearest transparent point and the opposite direction (When I think about it the opposite direction only should also work). So we divide the current height of the pixel throught the radius of the branch. We get the local height of the branch. Then we put this into the equation for the circle x^2+y^2=1 and we have it. The result is then the following texture:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/newnormalmap.png[/img]

This looks better and more precisely compared to the old one:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/oldnormalmap.png[/img]

Here are also some in game screenshots:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot105.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot98.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot100.jpg[/img]

So that's it for today.

notes.title: Development Blog #11 - Normal maps
notes.content:
Hello and welcome back!

Oh my god, yesterday there was really a severe storm in germany. It nearly blew my smartphone out of my hands. I was really lucky to arrive at home before they stopped the local train traffic.

Nevertheless we continued. What did we do in the last days? Ok first we did bug testing. We got the hint that the chests are removed when walking around. Ok we created a test map to find this bug:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot58.jpg[/img]

There was indeed a bug which affected the case when you get out of sight and then return to the box. But I am not completely sure if this is the bug which was reported. I checked it with the test level and no box disappeared. We will see...

And then we implemented our own normal generation algorithm. We did this because we also want to add parallax mapping and perhaps some advanced stuff. So our normal generation algorithm is also encoding the bump map height in the alpha channel of the normal map. So we can relatively easy add new rendering algorithms. We are finally using a Sobel 5x5 filter for our main normal map. Here are some screenshots of the normal map which was generated with our program and not with GIMP:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot68.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot67.jpg[/img]

 

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot72.jpg[/img]

 

 

The shadow is a little bit stronger.

And we also generated a normal map for the plants:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot74.jpg[/img]

Here we blured the plants and then combined it with the fine structures. This again was then the input for our normal mapping algorithm. But I admit that the bump mapping for the plants is not so visible as the normal map of the solid materials.

And we are also currently working on a new configuration dialog. I never liked the start dialog. And as we want to improve the renderer in the future there will be lots of different settings. To handle this efficiently we want to use an automatic generated UI.

And there is also a strange bug which brings the main lightmap to change to black. We will find a solution. And there was also a bug where the lod of the depth map was different as the lod of the world. We changed it now so that every view uses the same lod!

And we also added a compass on top of the screen:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/compass.jpg[/img]

And the ferns are now also moving in the wind!

There was indeed a bug which affected the case when you get out of sight and then return to the box. But I am not completely sure if this is the bug which was reported. I checked it with the test level and no box disappeared. We will see...

And then we implemented our own normal generation algorithm. We did this because we also want to add parallax mapping and perhaps some advanced stuff. So our normal generation algorithm is also encoding the bump map height in the alpha channel of the normal map. So we can relatively easy add new rendering algorithms. We are finally using a Sobel 5x5 filter for our main normal map. Here are some screenshots of the normal map which was generated with our program and not with GIMP:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot68.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot67.jpg[/img]

 

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot72.jpg[/img]

 

 

The shadow is a little bit stronger.

And we also generated a normal map for the plants:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/screenshot74.jpg[/img]

Here we blured the plants and then combined it with the fine structures. This again was then the input for our normal mapping algorithm. But I admit that the bump mapping for the plants is not so visible as the normal map of the solid materials.

And we are also currently working on a new configuration dialog. I never liked the start dialog. And as we want to improve the renderer in the future there will be lots of different settings. To handle this efficiently we want to use an automatic generated UI.

And there is also a strange bug which brings the main lightmap to change to black. We will find a solution. And there was also a bug where the lod of the depth map was different as the lod of the world. We changed it now so that every view uses the same lod!

And we also added a compass on top of the screen:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/compass.jpg[/img]

And the ferns are now also moving in the wind!

notes.title: Development Blog #10 - Bump Mapping
notes.content:
Hey and welcome back!

A new version of our game has been uploaded to the unstable branch. Check it out!

What has been changed:
[b]Version 1.2.3 Release 1053[/b]
[list][*][u]implemented animated grass[/u][/*][*][u]implemented bump mapping[/u][/*][*][u]created bump mapping for default main texture[/u][/*][*][u]added future support for specular mapping[/u][/*][*][u]added nvidia optimus flag[/u][/*][*][u]added ati high performance flag[/u][/*][*][u]corrected paper and camp fire recipe[/u][/*][*][u]added assert which prevents a camp fire similar bug to occur ever again[/u][/*][*][u]corrected recipes: no more mass increase when crafting[/u][/*][*][u]alpha sorting implemented[/u][/*][*][u]improved speed of particle system[/u][/*][*][u]implemented internal normal map generator[/u][/*][/list]
What is important for the speed of the game is the NVIDIA Optimus flag. When a game starts on a computer with NVIDIA Optimus and does not use this flag it will not use the high end graphics card. It will instead run on the slow one. This of course greatly reduces the speed. With this flag the high end card is selected.

If you have an old nvidia graphics card driver you must nevertheless activate it via the nvidia settings.

Then we also added bump mapping! Yes finally. It was pretty easy as we only need to change the way the normals are retrieved in our deferred renderer. And of course we had to calculate the tangent space for every polygon. Here are some screenshots:

[img]http://media.indiedb.com/images/games/1/23/22225/screenshot49.jpg[/img]

[img]http://media.indiedb.com/images/games/1/23/22225/screenshot54.jpg[/img]

[img]http://media.indiedb.com/images/games/1/23/22225/screenshot53.jpg[/img]

And here is also a video:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1ewHrIAiQew&feature=youtu.be

The bump mapping is currently only activated for voxel and solid blocks because we currently only created a normal map for this texture. The normal map was created with GIMP. In the future we want to use our own normal map generation algorithm.

Enjoy the new version!

notes.title: Development Blog #8 - Siegfried's Axe and Glass
notes.content:
Welcome back!

I hope you liked the unstable release. What was disabled in this build because it didn't worked correctly is „Siegfrieds Axe“. Now we can show you the first screenshots. What is so special about this axe? It adapts to the form of the tree. This means you can remove a one meter layer of wood in a single step. Crafting is necessary if you want to use this axe. You will still start with the old one.

Here are some screenshot (before applying the axe):

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot45.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot46.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot48.jpg[/img]

Look how it adapts to the wood voxels!

And here is a screenshot which shows how it looks after you applied the axe:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot49.jpg[/img]

There are no remains on the sites! Is this cool?

What currently makes us problems is the glass. It needs to be integrated in the deferred renderer. And as glass is transparent it needs to be sorted so that it is drawn in the correct order. Currently we are working on this. This means that we have to split the glass mesh into triangles, then sort the individual triangles and then pack them again before sending them to the GPU. And this has to be done every frame! This is currently not working. Here are some screenshots of the unsorted glass:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot50.jpg[/img]

Glass with shadow (I like this!):

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot51.jpg[/img]

Looks nice, or?

Should we make the glass more transparent? What do you think?

notes.title: Development Blog #7 and unstable release
notes.content:
Hello and welcome back

This time we have a surprise for all of you who bought the game. We thought that it is stupid when everyone needs to wait for the next release. So we created a new branch on Steam. The „unstable“ branch will always feature the current development version. It can be selected by:

Right clicking on the game in Steam
Selecting „Properties“
Go to the beta tab
Select the „unstable“ branch.

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/unstable.jpg[/img]

Our primary goal is to increase the contact with our players. You can give us feedback regarding the current version and we will then try to improve the game. And you can of course play the latest version of our game!

So before we released the game we did a lot of bug testing. What is most important is that the wheat is now better distributed so that the players can bake their own breads as soon as possible. Bread is necessary to regenerate your health. Here is a screenshot of our wheat:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot381.jpg[/img]

If you collect it you get wheat seed. You can bake a bread with it by using the table or you can plant the bread again. It is adviced to create your own wheat farm.

And we also updated the big trees which appear deeper in the forest:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot401.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot41.jpg[/img]

And we want to create a demonstration map where we will show all features of the game. Here are the first screenshots:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot361.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot37.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot441.jpg[/img]

And we also improved the speed of the deferred renderer. Specifically we reduced the memory consumption by the factor 2. This will reduce cache misses. We in fact used an OpenGL floating point buffer for the normals. But this is a waste of memory as it is possible to encode a normal in a normal rgb buffer.

And do not forget to select your high end graphics card if you have a laptop with NVIDIA Optimus! I forget this and then I ask myself why the game only had 20-40 FPS.

notes.title: Development Blog #6
notes.content:
Hello and welcome back. In the last days we updated the gameplay.

The first thing was the combat system. Precisely we wanted to give the player more feedback, when he hits a monster. In the current release it is only via a sound and this does not work corretly as there is a bug in the sound system. So essential there is no feedback when the player hits a monster. Sorry for this!

Audio feedback

So now we added audio feedback when you hit a monster. We also corrected the sounds when you only hit air. Then we also corrected a bug which moved the hand in a „unnatural“ position.

Physical feedback

We also added code which pushes a monster back when you hit it. This is dependend on the damage and on the mass of the monster. We also added an upper limit for the impulse. In the first tests small spiders where blown though the landscape by one hit.

Particle effects

And we also added a simple particle effect when a monster is hit. But enough of the words here is how it looks like:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot321.jpg[/img]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U8UnMnvGhjw

And we also made it so that when the health bar is displayed you will hit the monsters when you beat it with a stick. In the current version the system will shot random rays and tries to imitate so the movement of the stick. This did not work very well so we removed it.

Health Regeneration

Health regeneration was only added because of the lack of medi packs. So we made the regeneration now much slower and added bread and health portions which can be used to heal yourself. This means we added another survival element to the game. Before exploring the landscape it is necessary to craft something which will allow you to regenerate your health.

And you can now use the new camp fire to „craft“ meat our of raw meat!

And we also made a video which shows the new gui:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hvqXiswH7O0&feature=youtu.be

notes.title: Development Blog #5
notes.content:
Yesterday we tested the „alpha test“ blocks. We mean with this in our case a block which uses the alpha test for rendering. Ok if you perhaps know OpenGL a little bit it is pretty easy to set up the alpha test. Only a few commands and a texture with a alpha channel is necessary. We already used it for all of the plants and trees. But this was a little bit trickier. If we would have simply activated the alpha test the result would have been holes in the surface as the algorithms who converts the blocks to polygons expects them to be solid. We changed this and also updated the system so that it is more fault tolerant.

With this we can now create the illusion of grids, railings, fences or grates:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot36.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot38.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot40.jpg[/img]

And today we tested and corrected the flip-flop(?). What is a flip-flop? A flip-flop can be used in a circuit to store a single bit. It has one output and two inputs contacts. The output outputs the current bit which is stored in the flip flop. The right input is the value to be stored. But it is only stored if the left input has a current. This way it can be controlled if a new bit is stored or not. Here is a screenshot:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot43.jpg[/img]

FF means flip-flop. Hmm, ok when I look at the screenshot which is input is what? Ok, I had to guess when I wrote this text. No that's not ok. I change the code.

Coding in progress ….

Ok now it's changed! The read input is now labeled with read:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot44.jpg[/img]
And we corrected the memory management under Mac.

Then I made a screenshot of the inventory with all of the basic recipes (and also corrected some of the icons):

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot39.jpg[/img]
These items are only a part of the items which can be crafted. I think this is impressive!

notes.title: Development Blog #4
notes.content:
Hey and welcome back!

Today we did a lot of bug testing and improved the Blender importer. Specifically we improved the loading code of the animations. As we are using COLLADA as file format and as Blender only exports the current animation we needed to find a way to export multiple animation in one model. For this we combined all animations in Blender into one animation and then exported the mesh. Then in our importer we cut the animations into pieces again and voila we have it. Here are screenshots of a fish we made for the game:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/fish1.png[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/fish2.png[/img]

And we corrected the "non-shader" rendering mode. It hasn't worked anymore as we changed the way how we updated the screen. The new system checks whether for example it is necessary to clear the Z-buffer or not. This worked very well with the shader renderer but it didn't worked with the old renderer. It is now up to date and working again:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot35.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Development Blog #4
notes.content:
Hey and welcome back!

Today we did a lot of bug testing and improved the Blender importer. Specifically we improved the loading code of the animations. As we are using COLLADA as file format and as Blender only exports the current animation we needed to find a way to export multiple animation in one model. For this we combined all animations in Blender into one animation and then exported the mesh. Then in our importer we cut the animations into pieces again and voila we have it. Here are screenshots of a fish we made for the game:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/fish1.png[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/fish2.png[/img]

The new system checks whether for example it is necessary to clear the Z-buffer or not. This worked very well with the shader renderer but it didn't worked with the old renderer. It is now up to date and working again:

notes.title: Development Blog #3
notes.content:
Hello and welcome back!

This time I am writing the blog with emacs. It's actual the first time that I use this editor. Just for fun: is anyone of you using this it?

Ok, last time there was a strange bug where the depth map wasn't updated. This means that new blocks didn't cast a shadow. But this strange bug only occurred when the torches casted a shadow and not when the sun light did this. And as the torches are using a cube map as shadow map and the sun light doesn't I suspected that the problem could be in the graphics driver and not in our game. And I was indeed right. We tested the game on several non Mac computers and everything worked fine. So it works on Linux and Windows but not on Mac. We will try to find a workaround.

It's actually quiet interesting how the shadow cube map is generated. The hardware we are targeting does not very well support the combination of a cube map with a shadow map and a framebuffer. So we are actually not using a real depth buffer with depth values. Instead we are using a cube map with RGB format and we store the current depth color-coded in the texture. This means that when the "depth map" is generated the depth value is color coded. In the lighting shader this value is decoded. Here are is an example how the depth map actual looks:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot18b.jpg[/img]

This also means we can't use the GLSL shadow2D command to evaluate the depth texture (because it isn't technical a depth texture). Instead we implemented our own Stratified Poisson Sampling algorithm directly in the shader. You can see the effects of this if you combare the shadow of the sun (which uses shadow2D) with the shadow of a torch:

Shadow of a torch:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot17.jpg[/img]

Shadow of the sun:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot20.jpg[/img]

And I also improved the speed of the GUI as I had the impression that the performance dropped a little bit when the new GUI is used. The problem here was that we were still using glBegin/glEnd which is rather slow and of course deprecated. We switched now to VBO's to draw the GUI. This of course would have improved the performance but I wanted more. To understand how this can be achieved you must understand that every draw command costs a certain amount of time. And this does not scal with the amount of polygons which are drawn with this command. So it is a good idea to draw as much polygons in a single command. We created a VertexBuffer in the drawing canvas which collects all polygons which should be drawn. Whenever the texture or the pen type is changed these polygons are drawn in a single command. The difference can be seen in the following screenshots. For illustration every single drawing command uses a different color. Here is a screenshot from the old system:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot13.jpg[/img]

It can be clearly seen that every letter for example has it's own color. So we have one letter equals one drawing command. And yes today is birth day party (because of the colors of the letters :-) )

Now watch the new system:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot91.jpg[/img]

Here you can see that the letters have usually the same color. This means that these are drawn in a single command which is much faster. The particle renderer using a similar system. Here is a screenshot of the finished GUI:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot14.jpg[/img]

I am curious which crazy YouTuber uses the two colored images to show how bad my game is :-): "Look guys this crazy dev made a blue/yellow GUI which changes the color every frame".

So I hope now that the GUI is fast enough.

notes.title: Development Blog #2
notes.content:
Hello and welcome back to my development block. Today we did a lot of testing.

The first thing are the ramps. Ok, if you have played the game you perhaps know that there are two different types of blocks: solid and voxels. The ramps where originally created only to work with solid blocks. Now we tried to adapt them to the voxels. The result can be seen here:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot32.jpg[/img]

Then I was send into the forest to record new bird and environment sounds. But it seems that today was the „fathers take there children to the forest“ day. Ok it took me a while to find a good place were only the birds could be heard. But as I started to record there was some crazy bird who was really annoying. And I wanted to record background sounds but this wasn't clearly the case. This bird ruined everything. So I moved on but this crazy bird seem to follow me or it was another bird who made the same sound. Ahhh! But I think I catched some good sounds.

Then I went back to my Mac and dealed with a bug in the grass growing algorithm. Normally when you remove dirt the grass should regrow. But nothing happened. So I inspected the „slow voxel update“ code. This part of the game does things like grass growing, plant growing, fire simulation, heat simulation and the removal of trees when the player removed wood from them. In this case the heat simulation algorithm fighted with the grass growing algorithm. I repaired this and also checked the general update algorithm. Here is a screenshot of the regrowing grass:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot1.jpg[/img]

And I also corrected an error where the axe was shown in the 3D view after loading even if something else was selected. Then I moved the position where the hints for the player are displayed to the bottom. And I also found a bug in the new glass rendering system. Screenshots from this will be published later!

And the camp fire: I promised to one of the users to add a camp fire. So here is it:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot2.jpg[/img]

This item can be crafted out of stone, wood and a little bit of coal. And the lighting radius is the biggest in the game. So this is now the strongest light source except for the sun of course.

Then I realised that the pickaxe does not completely receive the light of the camp fire:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot4.jpg[/img]

To understand why this is the case you must remember that I use a deferred rendering system.  A stupid deferred rendering system uses spheres around the light sources. These spheres are rendered with a lighting shader. But I did not liked this approach as this needs a lot of polygons. My system uses instead the bounding box of the light source and then projects it into screen space. From this bounding box a bounding rectangle is calculated. This is the part of the screen where the lighting shader must be applied. It would now be easy to paint this without the depth buffer but I did not wanted this. Imagine for example a light source behind a wall. Without a depth buffer it would be rendered. This of course would not be visible as the shader would detected that the surface does not need to receive light. But it costs GPU cycles! So additional to the bounding rectangle the system also calculates the minimum z value and then renders the bounding rectangle into the 3D view.

Now what is the minimum z-distance of the light source if you are stand right next to it? It is zero of course. But normally everything behind the near plane is clipped away. And this is the case if you render a bounding rectangle with zero z-distance. It simply lies behind the near view plane. To prevent this the game moves the z position of the bounding rectangle a little bit above the view plane and then renders it. But this was in this case to much. So the parts of the axe which where nearer to the view plane than the minimum z-distance did not receive any light. I corrected the threshold and now it works fine:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot6.jpg[/img]

But such errors are very hard to find.

But the next bug is already waiting. The depth maps are not updated when you place something into the world. This means that new blocks do not create shadows which is very annoying. And the crazy thing is that the engine correctly triggers the depth map update process. And when I make a „screenshot“ of the generated depth map it all looks correct. New blocks are displayed there. The new blocks appear in the OpenGL framebuffer but not in the dynamic texture which was bound to it. Ok perhaps I need an OpenGL debugger.

So that's it for today!

notes.title: Development Blog #1
notes.content:
Hello and welcome to my development blog. I thought it would be nice to show you more of the development process.

In the last months we added a new UI, shapes, a canyon generator, a new font renderer, texture compression, a system which prevents data lose in case of crash, dynamic lights, glass, grids and a lot of minor improvements. We also created a changelog.

Here are some screenshots of the new gui:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot9.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot10.jpg[/img]

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot11.jpg[/img]

On wednesday I choose to merge the 1.2.3 and the 1.3.0 development branch. Originally we only planned to release the version 1.2.3. But I think my graphics designer wants to see his wolf model as soon as possible in the game and blender loading support is only in the 1.3.0. So I merged it. This was a lot of work. I thought it would be easier to merge different branches. But now we have a working version with both of the features of 1.2.3 and 1.3.0. The status of the Blender importer is that everything works with normal models except for the animations. I say normal because my graphics designer used some crazy fancy stuff in Blender to animate this model (inverse kinematics). We will see how we will get this into the game.


Yesterday I did a lot of bug testing and changed minor things. We got good reviews for the 0.1.1 release and now bad reviews for the new version. We thought that one reason could be that a lot of functions are not available any more instantly when you start a new game. The most important feature of the game are the small voxel. So to emphasize this I added to the selection box a grid so that everyone can see that the voxels are in fact very small:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot28.jpg[/img]

And you now also have instant access to all shapes when you start a new game. We originally changed this because a lot of Youtubers changed the pen setting in the first version of the game and then did not realised how to set it back. So they created very strange things in game :-).If you select now a shape you can change the size by right clicking. What costed me a lot of time yesterday was the selection of the shape. Ok this game has a system which allows the player to use an item. This can be for example a block or a tool. Until now only one item could be equipped at one time. But the current shape is just another entity which can be equipped. So to use a tool with a certain shape it is necessary that the player can select both. This already worked in the 1.3.0 version but it was broken by the merge. But now it works again. Ahh, look at the new big shapes:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/screenshot29.jpg[/img]

And I synthesized a new texture for the camp fire. Here is a screenshot from within our own 3D editor:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/editor.jpg[/img]

Before we published this project I implemented a texture synthesis algorithm for the creation of textures. It takes a photo as input and then creates a seamless texture as the result. I know that gimp also has such a plugin but by making our own we can add new things to the algorithm when we need it.And then we also created the icons for the shapes in blender. 

Here is a screenshot:

[img]http://www.staudsoft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/bar.jpg[/img]

And yes the next version will feature ramps. We already have a cylinder but it is a little buggy. The new shapes in fact use a CSG (Constructive Solid Geometry) algorithm which combines and merges the polygons of the different blocks. This was also a problem when we started the project. We wanted to keep the poly count as low as possible as we knew that our game would see a lot of them. So we merged them whenever possible. For blocks this is relative easy. This can be done in the world matrix. But for complex shapes like ramps or cylinder a general merging algorithm is necessary (which works on the polygons and not on the world matrix). So when you create a ramp of 1 meter in the game it first consists of a lot of polygons. When the CSG algorithm is finished only 4 polygons will be left which of course improves the rendering speed.

Today I digged in a lot of mathematical algorithms. I have a certain problem in the game which can be solved by data mining. But most of these algorithms need to have input parameters from the user which is not possible in a game. We well see. It could be possible to start the algorithm with a lot of different input parameters and choose the best result. But the speed? We will see!

And the MAC port. It is working with one exception: The configuration dialog. For this we used wxWidget and for the rest of the game SDL. This means when you start the game a normal wxWidget window is created and when you click start wxWidget is completely disabled and SDL is started. This works fine on Windows and on Linux. But not on Mac! And we don't know why. And should we even try to repair it or should we instead create an ingame configuration window? This are the things which we have to discuss.

And I changed the health system of the blocks. You can now dig faster when the amount of material you intend to dig is not very much. For example if you dig only one voxel it will now go almost instandly. But if you dig one 1 m block it will take as usual.

And Steam has answered: They really can't change the game back to EA.

So that's it for today. Enjoy the screenshots!
